name: Scrapwall Faceguard MK-0
description:
A salvaged half-face shield cobbled from reclaimed industrial polycarbonate, corrugated sheet steel, and strips of chemical-resistant gasket rubber. The surface is scratched and acid-pocked, with mismatched bolt hardware and improvised foam padding taped inside with medical adhesive. Usually grey or rust-orange from oxidation, sometimes with crude spray tags from Shelf crews.

The lower face panel pivots upward on a repurposed hinge, locking with a bent wire clasp. The eye slit is reinforced with a strip of cracked welding glass that filters UV but not much else.
functionality: Provides basic protection against acid splash, flying debris, and blunt strikes. The pivoting lower panel allows eating or speaking without full removal. Welding glass strip reduces UV glare from the Shelf's exposed smelting operations.
what_it_says: You build what you need from what you find, and you don't expect anyone to give you better.
story_hooks: A specific bolt pattern on the cheekguard matches hardware from a collapsed MagRail support — someone knows which section fell and when.
The welding glass strip is tinted a rare amber color only produced by one now-defunct Shelf foundry, making this a potential artifact or evidence.
The spray tag on the forehead plate is a Shelf crew mark for a gang that officially doesn't exist anymore — but someone is still wearing their colors.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist half-face shield that sits like a riot visor, dominating the upper face and cheeks. Angular, industrial, looks like it was torn from a construction site and reassembled by someone who needed protection more than aesthetics. Asymmetrical edges and visible seams give it a menacing, jury-rigged appearance.
physical_description.fit: Sits snug against the skull and upper face, held by friction and improvised straps (likely salvaged webbing or wire). The pivoting lower panel can be flipped up to cover the nose and mouth, or locked down for full lower-face protection. Slight pressure-points from uneven padding.
physical_description.primary_material: Reclaimed industrial polycarbonate (main shield), corrugated sheet steel (reinforcement), chemical-resistant gasket rubber (sealing strips), cracked welding glass (eye slit insert)
physical_description.texture: Heavily scratched and pitted surface with visible acid damage and oxidation. Rough, unfinished edges. Medical tape visible at seams where padding is affixed. Bolt hardware shows corrosion and misalignment. Welding glass insert is spider-webbed with cracks.
physical_description.color_scheme: Predominant grey-to-rust-orange from oxidation and age. Occasional crude spray tags in faded white, neon yellow, or gang colors. Darker stress marks and burn scorches around the hinge mechanism. Medical tape appears dingy beige or yellowed.
physical_description.closures: Pivoting lower panel secured by a bent wire clasp (manual lock). No traditional straps visible—likely held by friction against the head or with improvised rope/webbing loops behind the ears.
distinctive_features: Pivoting lower-face panel that can be flipped up or locked down
Cracked welding glass eye slit (UV-filtering but translucent)
Mismatched and corroded bolt hardware across seams
Medical adhesive and foam padding (unevenly taped inside)
Spray-tagged with crew markers and graffiti
Visible acid and oxidation pitting across entire surface
Bent wire clasp mechanism for panel lock
Corrugated steel reinforcement visible at edges
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage — pure ungoverned-shelf fabrication. No polish, no safety certifications, no corporate branding. Built from found materials in a scrap yard or Shelf workshop.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by scroungers, Shelf dwellers, industrial salvage workers, and street-level enforcers in the GLMZ underbelly. Signals survival, desperation, blue-collar hazard work, or crew affiliation. Suggests exposure to chemical/industrial hazards and a person comfortable operating outside corpo infrastructure.
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually weathered and damaged. Never pristine. Appears to have been through multiple near-death situations. Wearer likely makes field repairs with more tape and improvised fasteners. May have fresh graffiti from recent Shelf crew activity.
